items.title: Tim Kelly Interview, 1979-03-26
items.q: I think Tony recorded with John Detroit, didn't he?

ctx.x: No, he is not. He's passed on. I hadn't talked to his wit or anything. I never did really know her. Now, that's a fellow who did something that most people don't realize. If you had to choose one musician in this country who really started the ball rolling right time, I'd say it was Tony Prentice. Because he got a couple of writers in New York interested in it. And he would record them with his band and his trio. And from that, they wrote a book. And you never know what will happen out of an idea of something…
Right. Well, I just... I think Tony recorded with John Detroit, didn't he?

Not that I know him. I forget the name of the clarinet player. I'd know it if you said it in a minute. But he was with Johnny before the recordings, if I remember correctly. And I don't know why I can't think of the guy's name. But he's one of those forgotten clarinet players who played very, very well. It seemed to me Johnny Harmon liked his playing. I was surprised when the records came out, how good the man played. A lot of times you forget about people.
